name: Chiari I Malformation
definition: Downward displacement of cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum, which may be incidental or associated with headache, brainstem/cerebellar symptoms and syringomyelia.

typical: Sensory or weakness symptoms when syrinx/cord disease is present

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is MRI-based and symptoms must correlate with anatomy.
investigations.MRI: MRI brain/cervicomedullary junction and spine when syringomyelia is suspected.

green: Specialist neurosurgical/neurological assessment for symptomatic disease
Observation for selected incidental stable cases
amber: Posterior fossa decompression is considered for selected symptomatic/progressive cases.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Shirah/Greeva neurological symptoms may be documented, but structural craniovertebral diagnosis remains primary.

patientEducation.summary: Downward displacement of cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum, which may be incidental or associated with headache, brainstem/cerebellar symptoms and syringomyelia.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, rapidly escalating pain or other listed red flags.
